slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to compare physician-physician and physician-patient telehealth, providing insights into societal-scale healthcare utilization relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective for toxicologist-physician consultations than for direct toxicologist-patient care.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare the health outcomes and costs of physician-facing versus patient-facing telehealth access points.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 100 simulation runs (Mesa/Python) across various scenarios, measuring health improvement, hospital admissions, and cost per patient.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated data and an incomplete model assuming perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and single medical problems per patient.

slides.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
slides.highlight: This research utilizes multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate opinion dynamics and conformity in large-scale social networks, contributing to the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Deep MARL models opinion dynamics to show how conformity in large networks promotes misinformation.
card.key_idea: A GPU-accelerated consensus and truth-finding game using general-sum other-play MARL and a learned attention layer to recover agent importance from graph topology.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Bluesky network subset; compared large social media networks against small hunter-gatherer networks to analyze collective accuracy.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: DyaPlex: Full-Duplex Speech-Motion Model for Dyadic Interaction
slides.highlight: DyaPlex enables simultaneous perception and generation of speech and physical motion in dyadic interactions, contributing to multimodal social perception of team states for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: DyaPlex is a streaming, full-duplex model for simultaneous perception and generation of dyadic speech and motion.
card.key_idea: A dual-tower Transformer coupling a frozen speech model with a trainable motion tower using dyadic token interleaving and time-aligned speech-motion RoPE for cross-modal synchronization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the 4,000-hour Seamless Interaction dataset against A2P and DualTalk using FGD, P-FD, and BeatAlign; results show state-of-the-art performance.
card.limitation: The autoregressive motion tower is the primary computational bottleneck, requiring context window reduction to achieve real-time inference.

slides.title: Face versus Body Tracking for Human-Robot Interaction: An Egocentric Dataset
slides.tldr: EGO-CENTRIC DATASET FOR IMPROVING HRI TRACKING STABILITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces a custom egocentric dataset and evaluates face versus body tracking to reduce identity switches in social robots, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A new egocentric dataset and evaluation comparing face and body tracking for social robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Optimizes tracking by combining extended temporal memory and appearance ReID, finding that ReID stabilizes body tracking but destabilizes face tracking due to profile angle sensitivity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 20 custom Furhat robot sequences using HOTA, IDF1, and IDSW metrics; optimized body pipeline reduced IDSW by 49% over baseline.
card.limitation: Limited to 20 indoor office sequences with a stationary robot and specific fisheye lens; real-time compute constraints were not assessed.

slides.title: A formal definition and meta-model for a machine theory of mind
slides.highlight: This work proposes a formal definition and holistic meta-model for Machine Theory of Mind, providing a framework for inferring partner intent relevant to ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: Proposes a formal definition and holistic meta-model for Machine Theory of Mind (MToM).
card.key_idea: A rigorous MToM framework based on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and AI to guide research and evaluate current state-of-the-art efforts.
card.evaluation: Examines current state-of-the-art efforts and empirical benchmarking methods; specific datasets or metrics are not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Personality Anchoring for Social Simulation: Linking Personality, Social Behavior, and Interaction Success with LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY ANCHORING FOR LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a personality anchoring pipeline for multi-LLM social simulations, demonstrating how personality traits like Agreeableness influence goal achievement and cooperative strategies. This is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Personality anchoring using known characters reveals that dyadic Agreeableness strongly predicts shared goal achievement in LLM simulations.
card.key_idea: Agents are instantiated as well-known characters (personality anchoring) rather than via trait prompting, then interact across diverse goal-driven scenarios using structured behavior strategy selection.
card.evaluation: 1,010 conversations across 7 goal categories; evaluated via LLM-as-a-judge. Results show high consistency (ICC=0.89) and a monotonic relationship between Agreeableness and success.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-as-a-judge scoring and pre-existing model knowledge of characters, which may introduce stereotypical biases and lack cultural diversity.

slides.title: What Is My Robot Thinking? Design Considerations for Transparent and Trustworthy Shared Autonomy
slides.tldr: ENHANCING INTENT ALIGNMENT VIA INTERFACE TRANSPARENCY
slides.highlight: This research explores how feedback modalities and information richness improve intent alignment and coordination in shared autonomy, supporting MOSAIC's goal of aligning human-AI intent.

card.one_liner: Feedback interfaces in shared autonomy improve intent alignment and coordination, with visual feedback being most preferred.
card.key_idea: Systematically compared visual vs. auditory modalities and sparse vs. rich information richness to determine how transparency affects user-robot coordination and trust under fixed autonomy policies.
card.evaluation: User study (N=25) across two manipulation tasks (shelving, sorting) using objective alignment/correction metrics and subjective Likert scales; results showed significant improvements over no-feedback baselines.
card.limitation: Full belief disclosure did not consistently improve trust or alignment, and rich auditory feedback was found to be overly distracting.

slides.title: From Shortcuts to Reasoning: Robust Post-Training of Theory of Mind with Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: ROBUST THEORY OF MIND VIA REINFORCEMENT LEARNING
slides.highlight: This research introduces Thinking-RFT to improve Theory of Mind (ToM) capabilities and higher-order reasoning, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: Thinking-RFT improves Theory of Mind reasoning in LLMs by overcoming dataset shortcuts via verifiable rewards.
card.key_idea: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) using Group Relative Preference Optimization (GRPO) with explicit reasoning chains (<think> tags) and verifiable rewards to ground ToM in causal factors.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four shortcut-free datasets (OpenToM, ToMATO, MMToM, MuMA-ToM) using Qwen-2.5 models; Thinking-RFT outperformed SFT by 6-10% across narrative, conversational, and multimodal contexts.
card.limitation: Models can still fail by mis-tracking target agents or selecting incorrect final options despite logically correct reasoning.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework improves proactive robot assistance in noisy household environments by combining Markov models with uncertainty-guided LLM reasoning. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight framework combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered when prediction confidence falls below a threshold.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new HOMER-Noise dataset against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using F1-scores; results show competitive accuracy and superior noise robustness.
card.limitation: Inference latency is significantly higher than baselines due to external LLM API calls.

slides.title: Uncertainty-Aware Intention Prediction for Human-to-Robot Assembly Teleoperation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework for intention prediction and mistake detection in assembly tasks using hierarchical transfer learning and conformal prediction, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A framework for robot assembly intention prediction using human-to-robot transfer learning and uncertainty-aware correction.
card.key_idea: Pre-trains MS-TCN++ on human demonstrations, fine-tunes on robot data, applies conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification, and uses VLMs to selectively correct low-confidence segments.
card.evaluation: Tested on 22 action classes; human-to-robot fine-tuning improved Edit score from 70.50 to 80.70 using only 16 robot demonstrations.
card.limitation: VLM correction adds latency hindering real-time use; evaluation is limited to a single platform and task.

slides.title: Individual Gain, Collective Loss: Metacognitive Adaptation in AI-Assisted Creativity
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework of selective metacognitive adaptation to explain how AI use redistributes cognitive effort, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: AI boosts individual creative satisfaction but reduces collective diversity through selective metacognitive adaptation.
card.key_idea: Routine AI use redistributes metacognitive effort, amplifying partner modeling and surface control while under-supporting originality evaluation, intent formation, and reflective integration.
card.evaluation: Theoretical framework synthesizing existing empirical studies on AI homogenization and metacognition; no new original experiments were conducted.
card.limitation: The framework is not yet empirically validated and relies primarily on evidence from text-based writing and ideation tasks.

slides.title: Voting Protocols as Coordination Mechanisms for Role-Constrained Multi-Agent Tutoring Systems
slides.highlight: This research explores how different voting protocols shape coordination and collective decision-making among role-specialized agents, providing insights into how ADAM-CHAT agents can align on a single action when multiple valid interventions are proposed.

card.one_liner: Voting protocols significantly influence coordination and final responses in multi-agent tutoring systems with role-constrained agents.
card.key_idea: Four specialized pedagogical agents (scaffolding, misconception, motivation, metacognition) propose and revise interventions, which are then selected via simple, ranked, cumulative, or approval voting protocols.
card.evaluation: 1,200 simulated interactions using SciQ and HumanEval benchmarks with six LLM-based student personas; results are descriptive and show protocol-specific coordination patterns.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-based simulated students and judges, potentially reflecting model-specific behaviors rather than real-world human learning dynamics.

slides.title: Distilling LLM Reasoning into an Interpretable Policy Tree for Human-AI Collaboration
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE POLICY TREES FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces Co-pi-tree, which distills LLM reasoning into executable policy trees to improve efficiency and interpretability in human-AI collaboration, specifically evaluated on Overcooked-AI. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates and the Overcooked-AI benchmark.

card.one_liner: Co-pi-tree distills LLM reasoning into an interpretable policy tree to improve human-AI collaboration efficiency.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop method distilling LLM reasoning into executable partner-behavior prediction and agent-action selection trees, iteratively refined via interaction feedback and natural language summaries.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in Overcooked-AI; showed 35.4% higher average reward, 77.7% fewer LLM queries, and 97.1% lower latency compared to baselines.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Vietnam's Vingroup Unveils Two Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: The introduction of a guide bot and a factory bot by Vingroup provides examples of humanoid applications relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Memory-as-a-Layer adapter to capture dialogue history and emotional context, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: A plug-and-play memory adapter improves conversational speech emotion recognition by maintaining dialogue-specific state at test-time.
card.key_idea: Memory-as-a-Layer (MAL) uses Titans-style neural memory to inject audio-token-aligned residual updates into frozen LALMs, trained sequentially after LoRA task adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, and MultiDialog using Qwen2-Audio, Audio Flamingo 3, and Ultravox-v0.4; showed consistent gains in WA, UA, and WF1.
card.limitation: Broader coverage across all backbone-dataset combinations and comparisons against other memory architectures are still required.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and human-centered considerations into robot behavior to improve social acceptability, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A motion control framework that generates socially-aware robot behaviors by modulating velocity and interaction distance.
card.key_idea: An MPC framework using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-based human motion prediction to implement four distinct behaviors based on maximum velocity and interaction distance parameters.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-experts using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR SAFE PHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that achieves high trajectory accuracy and zero steady-state error during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Analytical feedforward cancellation reduces the robot to a constant-state linear double integrator, enabling a fast convex QP with Kalman-augmented disturbance estimation.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a 7-DOF Franka FR3; achieved <0.05mm steady-state error vs 44.8mm for classical impedance under 15N force.
card.limitation: Validated only in simulation; physical hardware demonstration and energy-tank passivity certification are listed as future work.

slides.title: OLIVE: Online Low-Rank Incremental Learning for Efficient Adaptive Exoskeletons
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for continuous personalization of exoskeleton control using on-body sensor feedback, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on adaptive AI coaching and human proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: OLIVE enables real-time, parameter-efficient exoskeleton personalization using low-rank incremental learning and on-body sensor feedback.
card.key_idea: Decomposes control policy updates into low-rank residuals with a gating mechanism for stability and a dynamic rank scheduler to adjust capacity based on terrain complexity.
card.evaluation: Tested with 6 participants across 4 terrains against static, rule-based, and fixed-NN baselines; showed improvements in smoothness (+13%), effort reduction (+22%), and stability (+15%).
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Video2Sim2Real: Full-Stack Autonomous Dexterous Skill Acquisition from a Single Human Video
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS DEXTEROUS SKILL ACQUISITION FROM HUMAN VIDEO
slides.highlight: This framework enables autonomous dexterous skill acquisition from human videos via a sim-to-real pipeline, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating and transferring procedural skills from ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: Autonomous framework for acquiring robot dexterous skills from a single human video via sim-to-real transfer.
card.key_idea: Refines retargeted trajectories using object-centric keyframe optimization and employs a decoupled policy: IL for global geometry adaptation and residual RL for local finger-level physics adaptation.
card.evaluation: Tested on seven everyday tasks; outperformed five refinement baselines in simulation and achieved 95.7% real-world success rate compared to 15.7% for FoundationPose.
card.limitation: Relies on heuristic keyframe detection, supports only non-articulated objects, and uses sparse keyframe refinement rather than continuous adjustment.

slides.title: The Josh Bersin Company Launches Bold Blueprint for Agentic AI: HR 2030
slides.highlight: The introduction of a blueprint for agentic AI is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on developing adaptive AI teammates.

slides.title: Agentic AI and Pedagogical Best Practice: The Tension Between Automation and Learning
slides.tldr: AGENTIC AI AND PEDAGOGICAL BEST PRACTICE
slides.highlight: This research explores the tension between AI automation and human learning, specifically discussing the role of metacognition and dynamic scaffolding in agentic AI. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and human-AI teaming to ensure AI supports rather than supplants human agency.

card.one_liner: Proactive AI agents risk undermining learning by automating the cognitive effort essential for deep understanding.
card.key_idea: A design framework integrating six pedagogical principles using intentional instructional friction, dynamic scaffolding fading, and teacher-in-the-loop oversight to prevent cognitive surrender.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper provides a theoretical review and an implementation matrix rather than empirical experimental results.
card.limitation: Over-reliance on AI automation can lead to learned helplessness and the loss of authentic human interpersonal connections.

slides.title: From 'What' to 'How' and 'Why': Sharing LLM-Generated Retrospective Summaries of Older Adults' Passive Tracking Data with Remote Family Members
slides.tldr: LLM-GENERATED NARRATIVE SUMMARIES FOR ELDERLY CARE
slides.highlight: This work explores using LLMs to transform multi-modal tracking data into context-aware narratives for remote family members, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: LLM-generated retrospective summaries of passive tracking data help remote family members monitor older adults' well-being.
card.key_idea: A multi-layer, multi-agent LLM framework that transforms multi-modal sensing data into insight-driven, context-aware narratives, moving from objective statistics to qualitative 'how' and 'why' explanations.
card.evaluation: Interviews and a comparative survey with 11 remote family members showed significant improvements in satisfaction, trust, and perceived helpfulness over initial versions.
card.limitation: Potential for ambiguous or underspecified inferences and information loss during multi-layer data aggregation.
